a4_benefit_business: Personalized automation recommendations increase consumer engagement with the Luminary app, driving higher device retention rates, reduced churn, and cross-sell opportunities for additional Luminary hardware.
a4_benefit_business_fact: Internal cohort analysis shows consumers who adopt three or more automation routines have a 42% lower 12-month churn rate than non-adopters.
a4_benefit_consumer: Consumers receive actionable, tailored energy-saving and convenience recommendations that reduce household energy costs and simplify daily routines without requiring manual configuration.
a4_benefit_consumer_fact: Beta participants who adopted AI-suggested routines reported an average 18% reduction in monthly thermostat-related energy spend in post-launch survey data.
a4_benefit_other_stakeholders: Utility partners and grid operators benefit from smoother demand curves when large numbers of Luminary consumers adopt energy-shifting automation schedules.
a4_benefit_other_stakeholders_fact: A pilot with Pacific Grid Partners in 2023 demonstrated a 7% reduction in peak-hour residential load across 12,000 enrolled households.
a4_benefit_public: Aggregate adoption of AI-driven energy efficiency routines contributes to reduced residential carbon emissions and supports state-level climate goals.
a4_benefit_public_fact: California Energy Commission modeling estimates that widespread smart thermostat automation can reduce residential CO2 emissions by up to 3% annually in participating regions.

a5_harm_pathways.cause: A misconfigured S3 bucket policy or compromised service account credential could expose occupancy schedules at scale, enabling residential burglary targeting.

a5_harm_pathways.actor: Luminary's advertising analytics partner (demand-side platform) receiving shared usage segments.
a5_harm_pathways.cause: Consumers who set up devices before the advertising sharing disclosure was added to the notice-at-collection flow lack knowledge that their home-behavior data informs ad targeting.
a5_harm_pathways.data_involved: Behavioral profiles derived from device usage patterns shared with advertising analytics partners without granular consumer notice.
a5_harm_pathways.harm: (C) Impairment of consumer control over personal information
a5_harm_pathways.source: Secondary use of profiling output for cross-context behavioral advertising disclosed only in the general privacy policy, not at point of device setup.

a5_harm_pathways.source: Media coverage of IoT data practices or a regulatory enforcement action against Luminary.

i1_processing_purpose: The Smart Home Usage Profiling activity collects device event logs, thermostat schedule data, motion sensor triggers, and app interaction data to build a behavioral model of each household's usage patterns. This model powers personalized automation suggestions and energy efficiency recommendations delivered in the Luminary app.
i1b_min_pi: Only device event logs, inferred occupancy patterns, and app preferences are used for profiling; full video footage and audio recordings are excluded from the profiling pipeline. Contact identifiers are used solely to associate the profile with the correct account.
i2_retention_detail: Raw event logs are purged after 24 months on a rolling basis; derived profiles persist until account closure, at which point automated deletion is triggered within 30 days.
i2_retention_period: Device event logs retained 24 months; derived behavioral profiles retained for duration of account
i4b_sources: Device event data is collected automatically from Luminary hardware (thermostats, locks, cameras, sensors) and the Luminary mobile app. Account identifiers are provided directly by the consumer at registration.
i5_admt_fairness_testing: The model is evaluated quarterly for accuracy drift and anomalous output distributions across geographic and device-type segments.
i5_admt_human_review: Automation recommendations are surfaced as suggestions in the app; the consumer retains full control and must actively accept or modify any suggested routine. No decision is applied without affirmative consumer action.
i5_admt_logic: The recommendation engine applies a gradient-boosted ML classifier trained on aggregated, anonymized device usage data from opted-in consumers. It identifies recurring behavioral patterns (e.g., typical wake/sleep times, peak energy usage windows) and maps them to predefined automation templates.
i5_admt_training_source: Training data consists of aggregated, pseudonymized event logs from consenting Luminary device owners collected over a 36-month period.
i6_vendors: AWS (cloud/ML), Amplitude (analytics), Zendesk (support), Stripe (payments), Veracheck AI (bias/ML auditing), and a demand-side advertising platform partner.
i7_external_consultees: Fielding & Marsh LLP (privacy counsel) and Veracheck AI (ML auditor).
i7_internal_contributors: Product Engineering, Data Science, Privacy & Compliance, Customer Experience, and Information Security.
i9_existing_dpia_summary: An internal DPIA covering the v1 recommendation engine was completed in March 2023 and approved by the CPO; it identified geolocation sensitivity and vendor data-processing risks, resulting in contract amendments with AWS and Amplitude requiring data minimization and deletion upon account closure.
